newsitem.title: LATVIA: BALTICS-MCDONALDS HOPES TO USE MORE LOCAL PRODUCE.
newsitem.headline: BALTICS-MCDONALDS HOPES TO USE MORE LOCAL PRODUCE.

text.p: Fast-food giant McDonalds on Tuesday said it hoped to use more local produce in the Baltics, including local meat and bread products.
The company said it plans to increase the share of locally produced products from the current 10 percent. This compares with Poland, where local produce is 98 percent.
"By the end of this year we hope to see local meat and bread products replacing imports," McDonalds Baltics manager Kevin Murphy told a news conference.
"The majority of supplies would then be coming from the local market," he added.
Riga Dairy currently supplies milk shake and ice-cream ingredients while the company sources lettuce in Estonia.
But he said that some $1.5 million of investment in meat processing and $800,000 in potato processing would be needed to meet EU quality standards, Murphy said.
"Our tonnage in the Baltics is not big enough for the time being for a local producer to see a return on it," Murphy said.
McDonalds is working on two solutions, including European suppliers entering a joint-venture with a local producer.
He said that processing products from Baltics in existing production facilties and re-exporting to the three countries was a solution which was currently blocked by local authorities.
"We are currently negotiating with our German meat supplier to make an investment in Latvia or elsewhere in the Baltics, entering a joint venture," Murphy said.
McDonalds European bread supplier, French FSB, has also expressed interest in investing in the Baltics, Murphy said.
